clue.text: Confused notice about following hospital systems for handling data

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so the word notice is rearranged
about means going round, so the rearranged word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A muddled announcement about following the hospital's procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTICE is rearranged as INOTEC, F goes inside it to make INFOTEC, and H is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Infotech is a short form of information technology, the computer and network equipment used to store and process information.

clue.text: Soaked female wearing second-hand clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the phrase for wearing second-hand surrounds the letter for female

blocks.note: in means wearing, as in a woman in red
used goods are second-hand
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A drenched woman in charity-shop garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for garments; it is a verb, so the phrase for wearing second-hand is wrapped round the female.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuse is to steep something in liquid, so an infused thing has been steeped.

clue.text: Superficial screening merely halved reproduction

indicators.note: screening means shielding or covering, so the word for superficial wraps around the next piece
halved means cut in two, so only half of the word for merely is kept

blocks.note: a facile argument is shallow and superficial
simply means merely or just

explanation.surface: A shallow film showing has cut a copy down to half its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' looks like a film showing; it means hiding. SIM is the first half of SIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact copy of a document or object, a replica.

clue.text: Maximum speed of boat in configuration of locks

blocks.note: top means highest or maximum, as in top speed
a knot is a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: A boat racing at full tilt through a canal's locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests canal gates beside the boat; they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a hairstyle with the hair gathered into a bun or tuft on the crown of the head.

clue.text: One maybe collecting lowers bloke into unruly crowd

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the word for bloke is placed within the other piece
unruly means disorderly, so the letters of crowd are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
he is a pronoun for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps gathering things to bring down, pushes a man into a riotous mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' looks like the verb to bring down, but it means animals that low, that is, cows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowherd tends and rounds up cattle, and cows are animals that moo.

clue.text: Anticipate abandoning everything in place of green growth

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so a word for everything is dropped

blocks.note: to forestall is to act in anticipation and get in first
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop looking ahead and give up everything for somewhere leafy.
explanation.walkthrough: FORESTALL loses its final ALL, leaving FOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area thick with trees, a place where plants and leaves flourish.

clue.text: After moving about, might fail to stop

indicators.note: once moved about, the letters of the word for might end up in a different order

blocks.note: might means strength or force
to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: Having shifted position, something may not succeed in halting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb of possibility; it is the noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreclose is to rule out or prevent something in advance, to bar it from happening.

clue.text: Gorilla in travelling funfair

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of funfair move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ape appearing as an attraction at a touring fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorilla' looks like an ape; it is slang for a heavy, a hired thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is slang for a brutish man or hired heavy, which is what a ruffian is: a violent lout.

clue.text: Suppress blasphemy perhaps outside empty little church

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outer letters
outside means around, so the word for blasphemy goes round the emptied word

blocks.note: blasphemy is an example of a sin, hence perhaps
first and last letters of little
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Stamping out irreverent talk outside an abandoned chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: To silence someone is to suppress them, stopping them from speaking or being heard.

clue.text: Confront authority about central element of boardroom’s make-up

indicators.note: the central element is the middle letter of the nine-letter word boardroom
about means surrounding, so the word for authority goes round the middle letter

blocks.note: to face someone is to confront them
power means authority or control
the fifth of nine letters is the centre of boardroom

explanation.surface: Challenging the bosses over how the boardroom is made up, in the sense of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks like the composition of the board; it is cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Face powder is a cosmetic dusted on the skin, one of the products worn as cosmetics.

clue.text: Left out densely packed material

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters of left are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tightly packed was omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is a fabric made by matting and pressing wool fibres together tightly rather than weaving them.

clue.text: Literature that’s certainly not true art?

definitions.text: Literature that’s certainly not true art?

blocks.clueFragment: Literature that’s certainly not true art?
blocks.note: surface reading: a sneer at some kind of writing that is not real art
setter's reading: a branch of learning (an art in the old sense) paired with made-up storytelling, which is certainly not true

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole it is the literary snob's dismissal of a genre; split up, 'art' is a field of knowledge and 'certainly not true' is invention, giving SCIENCE FICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a literary genre of imagined futures and technology, invented stories built around scientific ideas.

clue.text: Doctor held up when starting late was aimless

indicators.note: something starting late misses its beginning, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
held up means raised or lifted

explanation.surface: A doctor delayed by a late start was wandering without purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' suggests delayed, but here it means raised; LIFTED loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to move along with no fixed course or purpose, so someone who drifted was moving without direction.

clue.text: Choose lines encapsulating doubt and shock

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as in a capsule, so the word for lines holds the doubt

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines
an if is a doubt or condition, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Picking a course of action that contains uncertainty and alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway is abbreviated RY in crosswords, and a railway runs on lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify is to thrill or startle, giving someone a jolt of excitement.

clue.text: Person providing money to secure opening of organisation?

definitions.text: Person providing money to secure opening of organisation?

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the backer's word grips a letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a funder supplies the cash
first letter of organisation

explanation.surface: A backer who stumps up money to get a new body off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: FUNDER holds O, and such a person may well be the one who sets the organisation up.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder establishes an organisation, often supplying the initial money that lets it begin.

clue.text: Impression surrounding English border that is damaging

definitions.note: the definition describes a harmful thing, where the answer is the harm itself

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the word for impression encloses the next pieces

blocks.note: a dent is an impression pressed into a surface
E is the abbreviation for English
a trim is a decorative edge or border

explanation.surface: A mark left around an English hedge that causes harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is not IE here; it belongs to the definition, the thing that does harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A detriment is harm or loss, or something that causes such harm.

clue.text: Get irritated about woman’s gushing output

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for getting irritated surrounds the woman

blocks.note: to fret is to worry or be agitated
she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Getting annoyed by a woman's effusive talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gushing output' looks like someone's emotional chatter; it is water.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshet is a sudden flood of a river or stream after heavy rain or snowmelt, a rush of water.

clue.text: Break formal procedure constraining power of medium?

indicators.note: constraining means holding in, so the word for formal procedure grips the psychic power

blocks.note: a rite is a formal ceremony or procedure
ESP, extrasensory perception, is the gift a spiritualist medium claims

explanation.surface: Interrupting a séance ritual that holds back the medium's powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a middle size; it is a spiritualist, whose power is ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or pause from effort or difficulty.

clue.text: Dispatched men to obtain answer for politician

indicators.note: to obtain something is to take it in, so the earlier words hold the letter for answer

blocks.note: sent means dispatched
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Soldiers sent off to get a reply for a member of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' gives OR, other ranks, a crossword convention for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected legislator.

clue.text: Out-of-stock product shortened career following complaint

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word for career loses its last letter
following means coming after, so the shortened word comes after the complaint

blocks.note: a beef is slang for a grievance
to career is to rush along, as is to tear

explanation.surface: A shop item that has sold out, after a moan about a cut-short career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-stock' looks like sold out; read literally it means made out of stock, the broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a drink made by simmering beef, essentially a meat broth, so it is made from stock.

clue.text: Officer of the law misrepresented alibi for felon initially

indicators.note: something misrepresented is put the wrong way, so the letters of alibi are rearranged
initially points to the first letters of the two words just before it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letters of for and felon

explanation.surface: A police officer twisted a criminal's alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is not a link word here: its first letter joins that of 'felon' to give the two Fs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court official who serves writs and seizes goods, an enforcer of legal orders.

clue.text: Fire over pit needed for grill

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word for fire reads from the bottom

blocks.note: to axe an employee is to fire them
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Flames above a hole, required for cooking on a griddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' and 'grill' suggest cooking; fire means sack, and grill means interrogate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them closely, which is to examine them.

clue.text: Angry with receiving contradictory responses mainly

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for with holds the other piece
mainly means for the most part, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: and means with or along with
no and yes are opposite answers

explanation.surface: Someone cross at getting replies that contradict each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed means irritated or cross, a milder form of anger.

clue.text: Fantastic icon I arranged for religious ceremony

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order, so the preceding words are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone has set out a marvellous icon in readiness for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like the shuffle signal, but every letter of it is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctification is the act of making holy or consecrating, a rite performed in church.

clue.text: Duke attacks, having succeeded earlier

indicators.note: earlier means further forward, so the letter for succeeded is moved up inside the word

blocks.note: fits are sudden attacks, as of coughing
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A nobleman launches assaults after inheriting his title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman; it is slang for a hand clenched to fight. The S of FITS moves forward a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes is old slang for fists, as in 'put up your dukes', so one duke is a clenched hand.

clue.text: Anybody let in, if “nipping back”, stays endlessly

indicators.note: the answer stays within the run of words before it rather than being built
back means the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of anybody to the start of nipping

explanation.surface: A doorman's rule: anyone allowed in for a quick visit ends up staying for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, anybodY LET IN IF NIpping spells INFINITELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitely means without limit or end, so it matches without end.

clue.text: Pay gunmen to challenge arrests

indicators.note: to arrest is to catch and hold, so the word for challenge holds the gunmen

blocks.note: to defy is to challenge or resist
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Bribing armed men to resist being taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunmen' suggests criminals; in crosswords it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray is to provide the money for costs, to settle an expense.

clue.text: Attacked camp

blocks.note: first meaning: struck by a disease, as a crop or patient
second meaning: showy, artificial and exaggerated in manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like a military camp that was attacked; it is the adjective for exaggerated manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected describes both being hit by illness and behaving in a pretentious, artificial way.
